prerequisites: Physics and analysis from previous bachelor years.
Maxwell's equations, boundary conditions, representation of vectorial quantities in time and frequency domain, concept of electromagnetic waves from the Physics course.

learning_outcomes.text: The student (with Electrical Engineering as major or minor) fundamentally understands how electromagnetic waves behave in space and time, including electromagnetic radiation.
The student can apply this basic knowledge in different domains.
The student can solve practical problems through justified approaches.

syllabus_topics: Relationship between waves - inductive and capacitive coupling
Perpendicular incidence on multilayer structures, study of shielding.
Oblique incidence on conducting planes and on dielectrics.
Analysis of inductive and capacitive coupling.
Calculation of voltage and current waves on a terminated transmission line. Calculation of impedance matching networks: analytically and using the Smith chart.
Analysis of reflection and transmission properties of plane waves.
Analysis of the properties of propagation modes in a parallel-plate waveguide with conducting walls. Analysis of the properties of propagation modes in a dielectric waveguide.
Calculation of radiation characteristics of elementary current sources and applications of the radio equation.

assessment_methods.method: Exam during the examination period (written, closed book, open questions)

assessment_rules: The exam is written and closed book. An extensive, structured formula sheet will be provided during the exam. The exam includes exercises of comparable difficulty to those covered in the exercise sessions and tutorials.
